question: What is the true essence of the seemingly inert world?
premises: Ocean-ness consists in movements of both wavelessness and waves.
This same principle is the essence of all.
The inert world has consciousness as its essence.
inference: Therefore the world, though appearing inert, is essentially consciousness in varied movement.
uncertainties: nistaraṅgataraṅgādi is metaphorical; whether it maps to specific states of awareness is not explicit.
plain_english: Ocean-ness is nothing but the play of stillness and waves, and this is the essence of everything. Even the inert world is, at its core, consciousness.
